_status: Web demo for the 'house' slide. Asset, threat, weakness and control follow the Module 2 learner guide's house table (pages 2 and 3). Likelihood follows the open ways in (0 → 1, 1 → 3, 2 → 4, 3 → 5); bands are this course's 5 by 5 bands. 'at' positions are on a 900 × 540 drawing.

asset.label: Your house and what is inside

weak.label: A back door with no grille

threat.label: A criminal group after ID numbers

weak.label: An admin page open to the internet
The vendor's default password
weak.control: a strong unique password and MFA

reduce.label: Encryption
reduce.why: Lower the impact: stolen records stay unreadable

scenes.title: Asset: something of value
scenes.text: Your house and what is inside. What would you lose?

scenes.title: Threat: something that could cause harm
scenes.text: A burglar. We cannot make burglars disappear.

scenes.title: Vulnerability: a weakness a threat can use
scenes.text: A window left unlocked, a door with no grille, a dark yard. Watch the risk.

scenes.title: Threat meets weakness
scenes.text: The burglar tries the ways in. One is open.

scenes.title: Control: a measure that lowers the risk
scenes.text: A lock, a grille, a dog. No weakness, no risk.

scenes.title: Same idea at the RSSO
scenes.text: Threat: a criminal group after ID numbers. Vulnerability: an admin page open to the internet, still on the vendor's default password.

scenes.title: The group gets in
scenes.text: Impact: 48,000 people's sensitive data exposed, a breach the office must report.

scenes.title: A strong unique password, MFA, no public admin page
scenes.text: Both ways in are closed: no weakness, no risk. Encryption lowers the impact if something still gets through.
